sourceNote.title: Login rate limiting
sourceNote.html:
Login rate limiting

Exploring the sign-in rate limit on a test environment with a throwaway account (tester@example.test).

  • After 5 failed passwords within 15 minutes for one account, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes.

  • The lock message says "Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." and does not reveal whether the account exists.

  • A successful sign-in resets the failed-attempt counter.

  • Unknown email addresses get the same generic error and also count towards a per-IP limit of 20 attempts per 15 minutes.

  • Password reset link still works while locked.

  • Observed: the 5th failure already showed the lock message, so the 5th attempt might count as locked instead of the 6th.

  • Open question: does the lock apply per account across devices?

bodyHtml:
Scenario: Account lockout after failed passwords

Test case: Lock triggers at the 5-failure boundary within 15 minutes

Purpose: Check the failed-attempt boundary for one account: below the limit (4), at the limit (5) and the attempt after it (6). This also clarifies whether the lock starts on the 5th or the 6th attempt.

Preconditions: Test environment is available. The throwaway account tester@example.test exists and has no recent failed attempts. It is not currently locked.

Test data:

  • Account: tester@example.test

  • Password: any incorrect password for the failed attempts

  • Time window: all attempts within 15 minutes

  • Sign in as tester@example.test with an incorrect password 4 times within 15 minutes. Record the message shown after each attempt.

  • Sign in with an incorrect password a 5th time within the same 15 minutes. Record the message shown.

  • If the 5th attempt did not show the lock message, try a 6th incorrect password and record the message shown.

  • While the lock is active, sign in with the correct password and record the response.

Expected result: Attempts 1–4 do not lock the account. After 5 failed passwords within 15 minutes, sign-in is locked for 15 minutes and shows "Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes."

Coverage notes: This covers the valid partition (fewer than 5 failures) and the locked partition (5 or more failures), with checks at 4, 5 and 6. Evidence from the note: the lock message already appeared on the 5th failure, so the 5th attempt might count as locked instead of the 6th. Confirm which attempt triggers the lock against the intended rule. The note does not describe sign-in behavior exactly as the 15-minute lock ends, and it gives no expected result for a correct password during the lock. Record both as observations. Open question from the note: does the lock apply per account across devices? It is not covered here.

Test case: A successful sign-in resets the failed-attempt counter

Purpose: Verify that a successful sign-in before the limit is reached clears the earlier failed attempts.

Preconditions: tester@example.test exists, is not locked and has no recent failed attempts.

Test data:

  • Account: tester@example.test

  • Passwords: any incorrect password, plus the correct password for the account

  • Time window: all attempts within 15 minutes

  • Sign in as tester@example.test with an incorrect password 4 times within 15 minutes.

  • Sign in with the correct password and confirm the sign-in succeeds.

  • Sign out, then sign in with an incorrect password 4 more times within the same 15 minutes.

Expected result: The successful sign-in resets the counter, so the next 4 failed attempts do not lock the account, even though the total number of failures in the 15 minutes is 8.

Coverage notes: Boundary-adjacent check: the 4 failures stay one below the lock threshold on each side of the reset.

Scenario: Generic errors and the per-IP limit

Test case: The lock message and the unknown-email error do not reveal whether an account exists

Purpose: Verify that responses do not let anyone tell existing accounts from unknown ones (negative case).

Preconditions: tester@example.test is locked, using the steps from the first test case. A second email address that is not registered on the test environment is available.

Test data:

  • Known account: tester@example.test (locked)

  • Unknown account: an email address that is not registered on the test environment

  • Sign in as tester@example.test while it is locked and record the exact message.

  • Sign in with the unregistered email address and any password, then record the exact message.

  • Compare the two messages.

Expected result: The locked account shows "Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes." That message does not say whether the account exists. The unknown email address gets the same generic error.

Coverage notes: Covers the invalid partitions "existing account, locked" and "unknown email." The note does not give the exact wording of the generic error for unknown emails, so record it as evidence.

Test case: The per-IP limit of 20 attempts in 15 minutes

Purpose: Verify that attempts with unknown email addresses count towards the per-IP limit, checking 19, 20 and 21 attempts.

Preconditions: All attempts come from one IP address with no recent sign-in attempts. Several email addresses that are not registered on the test environment are available.

Test data:

  • Unknown email addresses (not registered on the test environment), any password

  • Limit: 20 attempts per IP per 15 minutes

  • From one IP, make 19 sign-in attempts with unknown email addresses within 15 minutes and record each response.

  • Make the 20th attempt within the same window and record the response.

  • Make a 21st attempt within the same window and record the response.

Expected result: Each attempt with an unknown email gets the same generic error and counts towards the per-IP limit of 20 attempts per 15 minutes.

Coverage notes: Boundary checks at 19, 20 and 21 attempts. The note does not say what happens once the per-IP limit is reached: the message, how long the block lasts, or whether the 20th or the 21st attempt is blocked. Record the observed behavior. Given the off-by-one seen in the account lock, check carefully which attempt is blocked.

Scenario: Recovery while locked

Test case: The password reset link works while the account is locked

Purpose: Verify that a locked user can still recover access through password reset.

Preconditions: tester@example.test is locked after 5 failed passwords within 15 minutes.

Test data:

  • Account: tester@example.test (locked)

  • While the account is locked, request a password reset for tester@example.test.

  • Open the password reset link.

Expected result: The password reset link still works while the account is locked.

Coverage notes: Covers the "locked account" partition for the recovery flow. The note does not say whether a completed reset ends the lock or resets the counter, so record what you observe.
